Investment by UTI in Essar
*101. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
FINANCE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn to the news-item appearing in
the 'Asian Age' dated 5th August, 2002 under
the caption “Special audit finds UTI invested
blindly in Essar”;
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government’s reaction thereto;
(c) whether Government would take any
action on the findings of the Tarapore
Committee in this regard; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Review of LNG projects
*102. SHRI  ASHWANI KUMAR: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) what would be the impact of the gas
discovered by the Reliance/NIKO
consortium on the viability of the LNG
projects currently under finalisation and
whether Government propose to review the
LNG projects in view of the new found gas
resources; and
(b) how much time would be required
for commercializing the natural gas
discoveries in Vizag and Surat?
Bansagar hydel power project
†*103. SHRI BALKAVI
BAIRAGI:Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to paucity
of funds and grave irregularities, work on
the ambitious inter-state Bansagar hydle
power project costing about three thousand
crore rupees  remained stuck up for about
14 years and now a target of two more years
has been fixed for its completion;
(b) whether it would be possible to
ensure the completion of such an ambitious
inter-state project during the stipulated time
period; and
(c) if so, the detials thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Priority sector lending for additional
areas by FIs
†*104. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH
‘LALAN’:
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of FINANCE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to include other additional areas in the
priority sector for lending by financial
institutions;
(b) if so, the details of these sectors;
(c) whether proposal for increasing the
percentage of provision of 40 per cent
lending to priority sector is also being
considered alongwith this proposal; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
International flights from Guwahati
*105. SHRI DRUPAD BORGOHAIN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Air India is
going to close the Bangkok flight from
Guwahati;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) whether Government propose to
connect Guwahati with some other foreign
cities by international flights?
Contingency plan of IOC for locating
strategic oil reserves
*106. SHRI NANA DESHMUKH:
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are working
on any contingency plan to deal with any
eventuality including blockage of crude
supplies from the Gulf;
(b) whether Government are thinking of
locating strategic reserves of crude oil in
some important locations of the country to
maintain undisrupted supply of petroleum
products;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether it is a fact that the Indian Oil
Corporation has submitted a proposal on
the need for having a strategic oil reserves
to Government; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Show cause notice against Reliance
Industries
*107. SHRI HARENDRA SINGH
MALIK: Will the Minister of FINANCE
AND COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Department
of Company Affairs based on the findings
of a limited inspection report has directed
the Regional Director, DCA, Western
Region to advise the Registrar of Companies
to issue necessary show cause notice and
other actions against the Reliance Industries
and to file prosecution for violation of
section 372A(2) of the Companies Act;
(b) if so, the details of action taken by
the Regional Director, DCA, Western
Region and by the Registrar of Companies;
and
(c) if no action has been taken, the
reasons therefor?
Scrutiny of balance sheets
*108. SHRI MUNAVVAR HASAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that balance sheets
of Ranbaxy, Cipla, DSQ Software, Padmini
Polymers, Sham Technologies are under

Removal of mosque from the airport
610. SHRI RAJU PARMAR: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned
"Airport mosque poses security threat"
which appeared in the Times of India, New
Delhi dated the 13th October, 2002;
(b) if so, what is Government's reaction
thereto; and
(c) what steps Government are
contemplating to remove the mosque from
the airport in view of increased security
threat to aircrafts landing at the airport?
Permission to foreign airlines for
enhancing passenger capacity
611.SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to open skies during the peak
winter season i.e. from December, 2002 to
February, 2003 due to rush in traffic during
the above period;
(b) whether Government are also
thinking of giving permission to some of
the foreign airlines to enhance their capacity
of passengers and frequency beyond the
bilateral rights;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the airlines to which permission has
been given?
Hindi/English newspapers and
magazines in IA
†612. PROF. RAM DEO
BHANDARY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the names of newspapers and
magazines in Hindi and English being given
to passengers on board in the Indian Airlines;
(b) what is the comparative percentage
of the supply of the newspapers and
magazines in Hindi and English;
(c) whether the percentage of Hindi is
quite low in comparison to that of English;
(d) whether it is in contravention of the
Constitutional rights of the official language
Hindi; and
(e) if so, the details of the proposal to
increase the supply of Hindi newspapers
and magazines?

Passenger facilities at
IGIA
613. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR
REDDY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have set three deadlines—September 30,
December 31, 2002 and March 31, 2003
for carrying out various improvements in
the facilities for passengers at the Indira
Gandhi International Airport, Delhi;
(b) if so, the details of the various items
included in the three lists to be completed
within the time-limit fixed for each;
(c) whether the various improvements
scheduled to be finished by 30th September;
2002 has since been completed; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Hijack attempt on Air
Seychelles
614. SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT
RAO:
SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the recent hijack attempt on
board a scheduled Air Seychelles flight from
Mumbai to Seychelles via Male has been
investigated;
(b) if so, what are the results of the
findings;
(c) what action has been taken against
those responsible for the security lapse;
and
(d) the steps taken to make security
check at airports more foolproof?
Purchase of New Aircrafts by AI for
US operation
615. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA:
PROF. M. SANKARALINGAM:
SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT
RAO:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Air India would
buy 17 aircraft for U.S. operations;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) what is the total cost involved and by
when the new fleet will be operational;
(d) the details of the total aircraft that are
in operation in Air India;
(e) whether Government have studied
the profits of U.S. operations; and
(f) if so, the details thereof during the
last three years?
Hijacking bid
616. SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have got the
reports from the Mauritius Government
about the recent hijacking bid by an Indian;
(b) whether it is a fact that the crew of
the Air Mauritius flight overacted and termed
the whole incident as a hijacking bid; and
(c) if so, the action taken to sort the issue
with the Mauritian Government?
